title: EU AI Office hits first hard deadline: frontier labs owe systemic risk files today
subtitle: Providers of general-purpose AI models trained above 10^25 FLOPs must submit formal systemic risk evaluations to Brussels by September 15 — the first binding paperwork for frontier systems.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: September 15, 2026 is the first substantive submission deadline written into the EU AI Act. Providers of general-purpose AI models whose training compute exceeded 10^25 FLOPs — the statutory threshold for a "model with systemic risk" — must file their first formal systemic risk evaluations with the European AI Office in Brussels today. The paperwork covers red-teaming methodology, energy-consumption disclosures, and compliance with the standardized copyright training summary template the Commission published in July. Enforcement of the underlying rules began August 2.

The threshold catches almost every frontier system on the market. GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5, Google's Gemini 3 series, Meta's Muse family, Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 Max, DeepSeek V4.1 and xAI's Grok 4.6 all sit above the 10^25 FLOPs line, and each provider is now on the hook for red-team results, incident-reporting workflows within 15 days of a serious event, and Article 55 adversarial testing evidence. Providers that skip the filing face fines up to 3% of global turnover; providers that file thin documentation invite follow-up technical audits.

This is where the EU's approach diverges most sharply from the US. Where the Trump administration on Monday called AI oversight a "SICK conspiracy," Brussels is now asking the same labs for line-item evidence that their models were stress-tested for bioweapon, cyber and autonomy uplift before deployment. It is also the first time a government has a formal file cabinet of what "safety testing" actually looked like at each frontier lab — content that until now lived only in internal system cards and voluntary disclosures. Any future EU enforcement action, and any leak, starts from those files.

For learners: the interesting number here is not the fine schedule, it is the compute threshold. 10^25 FLOPs is roughly the training budget of GPT-4, meaning every leading model launched since 2023 sits above it — Europe drew its regulatory line right at the current frontier and moves it up automatically. Anyone thinking about AI careers should read what a systemic-risk evaluation actually contains, because model-safety documentation is on its way to becoming a distinct profession, the way SOC 2 audits and financial disclosures did.
